rules.title: NJ residential rental application fee capped at $50
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes that exceeds $50. The cap is subject to annual CPI adjustment, covered in a separate rule. Penalties of up to $500 for a first offense, $750 for a second and $1,000 for each subsequent offense apply, with the wrongfully charged amount remitted to the applicant.

rules.key_value: 50 USD (base amount, before annual CPI adjustment)
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to a dwelling unit located in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent, or to a New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensee unless the licensee is the landlord of the residential rental property.
rules.interaction: The $50 base figure is adjusted annually by the Director of Consumer Affairs based on CPI changes, so the current-year cap may exceed $50.

rules.title: NJ application fee cap adjusted annually by CPI
rules.requirement: Beginning January 1 of the year next following enactment and each year after, the fee limitation is adjusted by the Director of Consumer Affairs in direct proportion to the percent change in the CPI (All Urban Consumers, NY-Northern NJ-Long Island, All Items) over the 12-month period ending October 31 of the previous year. The adjustment is made only if the percent change is greater than zero. The State Treasurer determines the adjustment by December 1, and the Director publishes the applicable limit on the Division of Consumer Affairs website.

rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the underlying fee limitation: one-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent, and Real Estate Commission licensees who are not the landlord.
rules.interaction: Modifies the $50 cap in the application-fee-cap rule. The current adjusted amount is not stated in the source and must be taken from the Division of Consumer Affairs publication.
